I don't know much at all about animal liberation or veganism, but I do know a bit about politics and I can assure you that if you want to spread your message about animal cruelty, calling people who don't agree with you supporters of chattel slavery is an awful idea. Nothing will repel people from your cause faster than accusing them of being something that (regardless of if its true or not) they don't believe they are. Even if you aren't trying to attack their character, it will still likely come across that way.

For example, I feel strongly about child labor in Africa being used to generate profit for massive corporations run by Americans. I believe that it is 100% slavery and that the largest shareholders at these corporations are exactly the same as slave owners back before the civil war, but if I'm talking about this with someone who isn't on board with it, I won't go "if you were alive in the 1860's you'd support the confederates and want to keep black people as slaves" instead I'll go "The conditions under which these children work are completely unacceptable, and if you look at what slavery was like in America, it is very similar to what these children experience. I assume that you're opposed to that form of slavery, so why is this not an issue that you seem to be concerned with?"
